One Outs game vs. Nakane (Ch. 1-2)
Lycaons player Nakane challenges Tokuchi to a game of One-Outs.

One-Outs is a simpler variation of baseball played by Tokuchi at the start of the series. It involves just a pitcher and a batter. The pitcher throws the ball to the batter and if the batter can hit the ball into the outfield, they win. It’s a game that also involves a lot of gambling, where people place bets on who they think is going to win in each round of the game.
But in this case, with Nakane challenging Tokuchi, Tokuchi proposes the following bet:
If Nakane can just hit Tokuchi’s pitch, Tokuchi will pay him 40 000 dollars.
If Nakane fails to do so, he will owe Tokuchi 40 000 dollars.

Tokuchi likely proposed the bet to create fear in Nakane. Nakane’s a young, inexperienced player, so it’s natural to assume he wouldn’t be able to handle a game with such high stakes. And this shows as the game actually starts. Nakane’s fear causes him to hesitate when the ball is thrown and as such, he fails to hit the first two pitches.

And for the third pitch, Tokuchi uses his grip on the ball to trick Nakane into thinking he’s gonna throw a forkball. And due to Nakane’s fear, he’s very willing to lean onto that possibility to win. As a result, he misses the ball again when it turns out it was actually a fastball Tokuchi threw.

Tokuchi’s strategy was an application of a psychological experiment in which a professional marksman was asked to hit a target. However, they placed a large priceless artifact just to the left of the target that you wouldn’t want to break, which caused the marksman to subconsciously avoid it by shooting on average a little more to the right of the target instead.

In this case, now that Tomosaka can see a bandage wrapped around Kojima, the young pitcher becomes, at least subconsciously, hesitant to pitch high and inside, due to the risk of damaging Kojima’s elbow and forcing him to retire. As Tokuchi puts it, “nobody wants to break a priceless artifact”, which in this case was Kojima’s bandaged elbow. This is why Tomosaka ended up pitching outside despite the catcher telling him to pitch inside, allowing Kojima to successfully hit the ball and get a home-run.
